steps.title: Draw the first side
steps.instruction: Type these lines, then press Run.
steps.explain: The turtle starts facing right. penup() lifts the pen to reach the starting point. pendown() draws again. forward(160) draws 160 units.
steps.expected: One blue horizontal line below the center.
steps.question: Which line chooses the length?
steps.answer: forward(160). The number is the distance the turtle travels.

steps.title: Turn one corner
steps.instruction: Add the turn and the second side. Run again.
steps.explain: left(90) changes the turtle’s direction by a quarter turn. A turn changes where the next movement goes.
steps.expected: An L shape: the bottom and right side of the head.
steps.question: Would right(90) draw the second side upward?
steps.answer: No. From facing right, right(90) points down.

steps.title: Close the square
steps.instruction: Complete all four sides and turns.
steps.explain: A square has four equal sides. Four 90-degree turns make a full turn, leaving the turtle facing right again.
steps.expected: A blue square centered on the grid.
steps.question: Which two commands repeat?
steps.answer: forward(160) and left(90) repeat four times.

steps.title: Name the square code
steps.instruction: Put the working loop in a function. Call it underneath.
steps.explain: size is an input. square(160) gives size the value 160 and runs the loop. We will use the same function for smaller squares next.
steps.expected: The same blue head. The call square(160) makes it draw.
steps.question: Which line calls the function?
steps.answer: square(160). The line starting with def defines it.

steps.title: Reuse it for an ear
steps.instruction: Add this call after the head.
steps.explain: The same square function now receives 24. Move to a new starting point before calling it.
steps.expected: A small square ear touching the left side of the head.
steps.question: Does square(24) change the head?
steps.answer: No. It draws a new square where the turtle is now. The earlier square(160) call keeps its input.

steps.title: Add the other ear
steps.instruction: Reuse square(24) on the other side.
steps.explain: The shape and size stay the same. The x-coordinate changes from −104 to 80 to place the ear on the right.
steps.expected: Matching square ears on both sides.
steps.question: Why do the starting x-coordinates have different distances from zero?
steps.answer: Each square starts at its lower-left corner. The left ear extends from −104 to −80; the right ear extends from 80 to 104.

steps.title: Draw one eye
steps.instruction: Move inside the head and draw a circle.
steps.explain: circle(12) uses a radius of 12: the distance from the center to the edge. Facing right, the turtle starts at the bottom of the circle.
steps.expected: One black eye in the left half of the head.
steps.question: How wide is this eye?
steps.answer: 24 units. Its diameter is twice its radius.

steps.title: Add a second eye
steps.instruction: Add a second circle at x = 40.
steps.explain: Only the x-coordinate changes. Both eyes have the same y-coordinate, so they line up horizontally.
steps.question: Which value would move only the second eye higher?
steps.answer: The 20 in its goto(40, 20). Increase it to move the eye up.

steps.title: Loop through both positions
steps.instruction: Replace the two eye blocks with this loop.
steps.explain: The list [-40, 40] supplies two x-coordinates. The loop first sets x to −40, then sets it to 40.
steps.question: How could you draw a third eye between them?
steps.answer: Use [-40, 0, 40]. The body will run three times.
